rows.predictor: enlarged_vs_reduced: indicator coded 1 when rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and 0 when rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is the covariate-adjusted enlarged-minus-reduced difference in expected day-14 chick weight

rows.note: Native effect: -0.1427209 g; SE 0.0899431 g. Test statistic: t = -1.5867906 with 284 residual df. Fitted n = 286 rearing broods (166 experimentally reduced and 120 unmanipulated), containing 1,978 chicks measured at day 14. Observation unit: rearing brood, identified by hatch_year jointly with rear_nest_breed_ID because numeric nest IDs recur across years. Outcome: median day_14_weight among measured chicks in each brood. Model: conventional unadjusted brood-level OLS, median_day14_weight ~ unmanipulated_vs_reduced. Design: comparison of experimentally reduced broods with unmanipulated broods; enlarged broods were excluded. Rows outside rear_nest_trt codes 6/7 and incomplete fitted variables were excluded (the fitted outcome was complete). The coefficient is the unmanipulated-minus-reduced difference in brood-median day-14 mass. No hatch-year adjustment was used. Important limitation: unmanipulated broods were not systematically matched to manipulated broods, so this is not a clean randomized treatment contrast.
rows.predictor: unmanipulated_vs_reduced = 1 for rear_nest_trt 7 (unmanipulated brood) and 0 for rear_nest_trt 6 (experimentally reduced brood); coefficient is 1 minus 0

rows.note: Gaussian identity-link GEE fitted to individual chick day-14 weight (grams), with recorded net_rearing_manipulation as a linear continuous predictor and categorical hatch year as an adjustment. An exchangeable working correlation was used within composite year-by-rearing-nest brood clusters, with brood-cluster robust sandwich uncertainty. The fitted sample was 2,716 measured chicks in 320 experimentally enlarged or reduced rearing broods; unmanipulated broods were excluded, as were 85 chick rows in manipulated broods lacking recorded net manipulation. Observation unit: individual chick. Design: brood-size manipulation analyzed as a chick-level, chick-weighted GEE. Native effect = -0.1799499482 grams per net chick added; robust SE = 0.0148866177 grams; Wald z = -12.0880344888; inferential df = infinite (asymptotic normal inference).
rows.predictor: Recorded net_rearing_manipulation, measured in chicks: positive values indicate net chicks added to the rearing brood and negative values indicate net chicks removed; focal coefficient is the linear change in expected individual day-14 weight per one-chick increase in this signed quantity.

rows.note: Chick-level OLS of day_14_weight (grams) on competition_score and categorical hatch_year. competition_score was +1 for experimentally enlarged rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=5) and -1 for experimentally reduced broods (rear_nest_trt=6); unmanipulated broods were excluded. CR1 finite-sample-corrected standard errors were clustered by year-specific rearing brood (hatch_year × rear_nest_breed_ID). Native effect = -0.508069880305 g per 1-unit score increase; cluster-robust SE = 0.0447542856745 g; t = -11.3524296645; inferential df = 332 (333 brood clusters); fitted n = 2,801 chicks. Observation unit: chick alive and measured at day 14. Design: brood-size manipulation comparing experimentally enlarged with reduced rearing broods, adjusted for categorical breeding year.
rows.predictor: competition_score: +1 for rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and -1 for rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is grams per 1-unit increase, so the full enlarged-minus-reduced contrast spans 2 units

rows.note: Outcome: mean day_14_weight (grams) among chicks alive and measured at day 14, aggregated to one equally weighted observation per rearing brood. Included broods assigned to enlarged (rear_nest_trt=5) or reduced (rear_nest_trt=6) treatment; composite brood ID was hatch_year:rear_nest_breed_ID. Exposure was reconstructed from movement bookkeeping as rear_Cs_in minus rear_Cs_out. It exactly matched net_rearing_manipulation wherever both were observed. Of 333 assigned enlarged/reduced broods, 13 lacked reconstructable exposure and were excluded; the fitted sample comprised 320 broods and 2,716 chick measurements. Model: OLS of brood-mean day-14 weight on reconstructed signed net chick movement and categorical hatch year, using conventional model-based OLS uncertainty. Native effect = -0.1823279393 grams per additional net chick added; SE = 0.0156424771; t=-11.6559505551 with 316 residual df. Observation unit: rearing brood. Design: experimental brood-size manipulation analyzed as a linear dose-response, adjusted for breeding year. Unmanipulated broods were not included because they were not systematically matched to manipulated broods.
rows.predictor: reconstructed_net = rear_Cs_in - rear_Cs_out, measured in chicks; a one-unit increase is one additional chick moved into rather than out of the rearing brood, so positive values represent more sibling competition

rows.note: Outcome: median day-14 tarsus length (mm) among measured chicks within each rearing brood. Observation unit and fitted n: 453 rearing broods, uniquely identified as hatch_year x rear_nest_breed_ID; these summarized all 3,720 measured chicks (166 reduced, 120 unmanipulated, 167 enlarged broods). Model: equal-brood-weight ordinary least squares, median_day14_tarsus ~ competition_score + categorical hatch_year, using the conventional model-based OLS standard error. Focal test: t = -7.606476565027 with 449 residual inferential df. Design: three-group brood-size manipulation represented by an ordered linear contrast. No outcome values were missing; rows lacking year or rearing-nest identity would have been excluded. The coefficient is in the native fitted scale of mm per one score step and assumes the reduced-to-unmanipulated and unmanipulated-to-enlarged steps are equally spaced in sibling competition.
rows.predictor: competition_score, coded exactly as -1 for experimentally reduced rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=6), 0 for unmanipulated rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=7), and +1 for experimentally enlarged rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=5); reported coefficient is the linear change in brood-median day-14 tarsus length in mm per +1 score step

rows.note: Outcome: mean day_14_weight (grams) among chicks alive and measured at day 14, aggregated so each year-specific rearing brood received equal weight. Model: OLS of brood-mean day-14 weight on competition_score plus categorical hatch_year. Groups included: 167 enlarged, 166 reduced, and 120 unmanipulated rearing broods; no treatment group was excluded. Fitted n=453 rearing broods representing 3,720 chicks. Observation unit: year-specific rearing brood, constructed as hatch_year × rear_nest_breed_ID because bare nest IDs recur across years. Design: brood-size manipulation experiment with the unmanipulated category included in an ordered linear contrast; unmanipulated broods were not systematically matched to manipulated broods. The score assumes unmanipulated broods are the midpoint between enlarged and reduced treatment-category scores. Native effect=-0.543029125665 grams per one-unit score increase; model-based SE=0.0475161924807 grams; t=-11.4282962779 with 449 residual df. This is a signed linear trend, not an omnibus statistic and not the full two-unit enlarged-minus-reduced difference.
rows.predictor: competition_score: +1 for enlarged rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=5), 0 for unmanipulated rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=7), and -1 for reduced rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=6); coefficient is grams per one-unit increase in this ordered score

rows.note: Outcome: individual chick day_14_weight in grams. Observation unit: each chick alive and measured at day 14 with nonmissing net_rearing_manipulation; fitted n=2,716 chicks in 319 rearing-brood clusters. Exclusions: unmanipulated rear_nest_trt=7, chicks outside experimentally enlarged/reduced rear_nest_trt 5/6, and rows missing outcome, hatch_year, rearing-brood ID, or manipulation dose. Model: chick-level OLS day_14_weight ~ net_rearing_manipulation + net_rearing_manipulation^2 + categorical hatch_year. Uncertainty: finite-sample-corrected standard errors clustered by rear_nest_breed_ID, with t inference; t=-11.5041676116, inferential df=318. Design: experimental brood-size manipulation analyzed with a quadratic dose-response. The focal native-scale contrast is fitted mass at dose +2 minus fitted mass at dose -2, holding breeding year fixed; the quadratic and year terms cancel in this symmetric contrast. Dose was net_rearing_manipulation, defined as chicks moved in minus chicks moved out. The fitted estimate indicates 0.66094 g lower day-14 mass at +2 than at -2 net chicks.
rows.predictor: Model-implied day-14 mass contrast for net_rearing_manipulation=+2 minus net_rearing_manipulation=-2, where net_rearing_manipulation is chicks moved in minus chicks moved out; breeding year held fixed in a model containing linear and squared dose terms

rows.note: Outcome: mean day-14 tarsus length (mm) among measured chicks within each rearing brood. Analysis included the 332 experimentally manipulated rearing broods identified by rear_nest_breed_ID (167 enlarged and 165 reduced), comprising 2,801 chick measurements; unmanipulated broods were excluded. Each rearing brood was weighted equally. The fitted effect is the unadjusted difference in brood-mean tarsus length between enlarged and reduced arms, with a Welch unequal-variance standard error. Test statistic: Welch t = -8.39498691077; Satterthwaite inferential df = 305.225579023. Observation unit: rearing brood. Design: two-arm experimental brood-size manipulation. Enlarged mean = 16.5282206709 mm; reduced mean = 16.9165266955 mm.
rows.predictor: Sibling-competition contrast coded +0.5 for rear_nest_trt = 5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and -0.5 for rear_nest_trt = 6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is exactly enlarged minus reduced.

rows.note: Outcome: mean day_14_weight (grams) among chicks alive and measured at day 14, computed separately for each rearing brood identified by rear_nest_breed_ID. Included experimentally manipulated broods with rear_nest_trt 5 or 6 and nonmissing day-14 mass and rearing-brood ID; excluded unmanipulated rear_nest_trt 7. Model: brood-level weighted least squares with an intercept and the signed treatment contrast; each brood's analytic weight was its number of measured day-14 chicks. Uncertainty: HC2 heteroskedasticity-robust SE across brood observations. Native effect = -1.01408397108 g; SE = 0.0896116277067 g. Test-statistic kind and value: t = -11.3164328897; inferential residual df = 330; two-sided p = 2.61908041152e-25. Fitted n = 332 rearing broods (167 enlarged, 165 reduced), representing 2,801 chick measurements. Observation unit: rearing brood. Design: two-arm experimental brood-size manipulation; brood-level WLS enlarged-minus-reduced contrast, weighted by measured chick count. The estimate is the measured-chick-weighted mean day-14 mass in enlarged broods minus that in reduced broods (9.76268656716 g minus 10.7767705382 g).
rows.predictor: Sibling-competition treatment contrast coded +0.5 for rear_nest_trt 5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and -0.5 for rear_nest_trt 6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); its coefficient is exactly the measured-chick-count-weighted enlarged-minus-reduced difference in brood mean day-14 mass.
